findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource shares the same timestamp
findings.body: The dataclass field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Because this is a plain default value rather than `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`, `timezone.now()` is called a single time when the class body executes (i.e., at module import time). Every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit `queued` value — including all instances created via `AssignmentSource.from_integration()` in the inbound sync path — will therefore carry the process's import-time timestamp instead of the time the source was created. If `queued` is ever used for staleness/freshness checks (which appears to be its intent), the value will be silently wrong. The fix is `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The new test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: No test coverage for deassign with a matching AssignmentSource
findings.body: The PR adds cycle-prevention logic for both the assign and deassign outbound paths (`GroupAssignee.objects.deassign` now accepts and forwards `assignment_source`), but only the assign path gets a negative test (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`). `test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign` only verifies the no-source case (`assignment_source=None`). If the `assignment_source` forwarding in `deassign` were dropped or broken, no test would fail, and an inbound Jira unassignment would again trigger an outbound unassign back to Jira, recreating a sync loop. A test mirroring the assign case — calling `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(group, assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))` and asserting `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called — should be added.
